subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase/stagger or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, and should heartbeat expose any public knob beyond its current automatic stable phase?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the remaining change defines public scheduling semantics and config/protocol shape, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive maintainer product direction.

options.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add a focused public contract for cron `every` phase/stagger with schema, CLI, persistence, docs, status display, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed and document heartbeat behavior
options.body: Preserve current fixed `everyMs`/`anchorMs` semantics and treat heartbeat's automatic phase spreading plus cron-expression stagger as the supported anti-herd behavior.

options.title: Accept broader prime mode
options.body: Add prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls for heartbeat and cron, with explicit migration, observability, and compatibility requirements.

recommendation.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add a focused public contract for cron `every` phase/stagger with schema, CLI, persistence, docs, status display, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current cron stagger history and is the best routing candidate for the public scheduling contract decision.
